state.request: Advise which generated application target CanLang should start with: JavaScript or WebAssembly on workerd. The user asks for the best outcome, with adoption primary. Do not confuse the language used to implement the compiler with the app artifact it emits. No implementation is requested in this consultation. Avoid treating a fashionable target or theoretical speed as evidence.
state.language: CanLang is an AI-authored, compact DSL for CRUD-centered business SaaS, permissions, workflows and managed Cloudflare services. D1, R2, Durable Objects, Queues and email are first-class capabilities. Server-rendered daisyUI/HTMX, inline locale messages and MCP share canonical operation schemas and authorization. Exact 64-bit int, decimal/money, deterministic type/effect checks, durable outcomes and inline BDD behavior are required. App source has no unrestricted general-purpose escape hatch. Heavy media/design/observability engines are outside v1. The repository has 44 source-design examples and a syntax parser, not a semantic compiler, runtime or execution benchmarks.
state.primary_evidence: Cloudflare Workers uses V8 for JavaScript and Wasm (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/web-standards/). The official Rust/Wasm integration emits a JS entrypoint, accesses platform APIs through wasm-bindgen glue, and bridges Rust futures to JS promises (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/languages/rust/#how-this-deployment-works). This makes Wasm viable for managed services, not incapable. Workers supports Wasm SIMD but not threading; Wasm deployments often include extra runtime code, with possible size/startup costs. WASI support is partial/experimental (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/webassembly/). Wasm can reuse existing Rust/C libraries and host a portable computation core; Cloudflare-specific service APIs still need host integration. None of these facts proves either target faster for CanLang.
state.correctness: The D1 API accepts JavaScript values: SQLite INTEGER is signed 64-bit, but BigInt binding is unsupported and JS Number has a safe-integer ceiling (https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/#type-conversion). Both targets need an exact storage/wire codec; generating ordinary Number arithmetic for every int/decimal/money field is invalid. Neither Wasm validation nor JS execution supplies CanLang permissions, transaction behavior, schema typing or BDD correctness. CanLang's checker and shared operation runtime must enforce them before/around emitted effects.
state.tradeoffs: JS can call the native platform API surface directly and use standard async request handlers. Readable output plus source maps can aid diagnosis; static CanLang checks remain compiler-owned regardless of dynamic JS representation. Wasm offers a reusable binary core, native fixed-width numeric operations and SIMD/library reuse, but also an app code generator/toolchain plus host-call/object/string/async integration to maintain. A hybrid keeps handlers/bindings/rendering in JS and adds a Wasm computation module, with two artifact kinds and a defined interface. No current CanLang workload has demonstrated a compute bottleneck needing that hybrid. JS also needs precise scalar helpers and managed-service adapters; fewer host boundaries do not mean zero runtime work. Claims about bundle size, speed or adoption must remain hypotheses without a CanLang benchmark.
state.scope: Select one canonical initial app target; no per-app backend choice, additional authored build manifest, speculative second backend, deployment wrapper or new DSL primitive. Compiler-generated SQL, binding requirements, HTML/CSS/assets and BDD artifacts are required outputs distinct from app executable target. A first runnable slice should execute existing CRUD, one guarded operation, server-rendered UI, the same operation over MCP, and its inline examples on workerd. Unsupported declarations must fail clearly, rather than be ignored to make a draft appear runnable. This scope statement is an implementation recommendation, not a completed result. A later internal Wasm helper could be justified by concrete library/workload evidence without exposing another SaaS syntax path.

target.instructions: Which initial generated application target best serves the supplied CanLang scope and adoption/simplicity goals while preserving exact semantics and credible platform integration? Compare the concrete benefits and costs of every alternative without assuming speed, safety or correctness from target name alone.

criteria.javascript: Emit JavaScript ES modules for workerd, with one versioned shared runtime and exact scalar/storage helpers. Favor direct managed-service/async integration and diagnosable output; accept compiler/runtime obligations and lack of an initial portable Wasm computation core.
criteria.wasm: Emit a Wasm application core with generated JS entrypoint and host interfaces. Favor binary-core portability, fixed-width operations and existing library reuse; accept toolchain/glue maintenance and platform-specific integration without a proven workload speed benefit.
criteria.hybrid: Start with JS handlers/runtime plus a Wasm computation module. Combine direct host access and compiled computation/library reuse; accept two output kinds, their interface and build integration before a CanLang compute need is demonstrated.
criteria.unresolved: Defer selecting the target because the supplied platform facts and workload scope do not justify an initial implementation choice without further evidence.
